slot.brief: A car negotiates a banked curve with friction; find the range of safe speeds or maximum speed using tanθ-based formula.

stem: A car moves on a banked circular road of radius $7.5$ m. If $\tan\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}$ for the banking angle and the coefficient of friction is $0.5$, find its maximum safe speed. Take $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.

verdicts.working: For maximum speed, friction acts down the bank: v²/r = g(tanθ + μ)/(1 − μtanθ). Hence v² = 10 × 7.5 × 1/0.75 = 100, giving v = 10 m/s.

working:
$v_{\max}^2=Rg\dfrac{\tan\theta+\mu}{1-\mu\tan\theta}$
$=7.5(10)\dfrac{0.5+0.5}{1-(0.5)(0.5)}=100$
$v_{\max}=10$ m s$^{-1}$

Independent check: For maximum speed, friction acts down the bank: v²/r = g(tanθ + μ)/(1 − μtanθ). Hence v² = 10 × 7.5 × 1/0.75 = 100, giving v = 10 m/s.
